key_insight: Neural quantum state training can be reframed as a trust-region reinforcement learning problem, enabling a new optimizer, PWO, that is both scalable and more stable than common baselines.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational physicists and ML engineers a practical way to train large autoregressive quantum wavefunction models without the cost and fragility of second-order methods.
method: Reinterpret variational energy minimization as an advantage policy-gradient objective over the Born distribution.
Apply proximal/trust-region updates by clipping amplitude probability ratios and phase increments separately.
Avoid explicit matrix inversion, enabling sample reuse across multiple optimization steps.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on Ising and frustrated J1-J2 spin systems in 1D and 2D, where it improves stability and wall-clock convergence over Adam, minSR, and SPRING, and is also demonstrated on a 1.5B-parameter RWKV-7 model.
watch_item: As with trust-region methods, performance may depend on careful tuning of clipping bounds and numerical stability in the amplitude and phase channels.
paper_title: One More Time: Revisiting Neural Quantum States from a Reinforcement Learning Perspective
